chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn 'Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali narrated to me from Ismail ibn Muslim al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who said:

The people of innovations (Bid'ah) will be brought on the Day of Judgment, and the Qadiriyyah will be seen among them like a white hump on a black ox. Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, will ask: 'What did you intend?' They will reply: 'We intended nothing but Your Face (pleasure).' He will say: 'I have excused your stumbles and forgiven your slips, except for the Qadiriyyah, for they entered into polytheism (Shirk) from where they did not know.'

key_terms.الْبِدَع: Innovations (Bid'ah), religious innovations deviating from the norm
key_terms.الْقَدَرِیَّه: Qadiriyyah, a theological group emphasizing divine decree (Qadr)
key_terms.الْوَاجْهَ: The Face (of God), metaphor for seeking His pleasure

ai.seo_question: Who are the Qadiriyyah and why are they singled out for punishment among innovors on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith highlights the Qadariyyah as a distinct group of innovators whose error is not mere deviation but a subtle form of *Shirk* committed in ignorance, distinguishing them from other sects. The metaphor of the white hump on a black ox signifies their conspicuous visibility among the masses of sinners, yet their specific theological flaw—denying divine power over human action—excludes them from the general pardon granted to others despite their sincere claim of seeking God's pleasure.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 6. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakil who said it was narrated to me by Musa b. Ja’far who said it was narrated to us by Musa b. ’Imran Nakha’i who said it was narrated to me by al-Hussain b. Yazid al-Nawfali from Ismail b. Muslim al-Sakuni from Abi Abdillah Ja’far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers from Ali b. Abi Talib (a.s.) who said: “

The people who do innovation (Bid-a’t) will be brought on the Day of Judgment in the same way as black and white bullocks are prominent. Qadiris will in the same way appear prominent among them and Allah, the Mighty and Sublime will ask: What was your intention? They will reply: Our intention was to seek Your pleasure. Allah will say: Your sins are forgiven but of the Qadiris are not. This is so because they committed polytheism in ignorance.”
